title: Unitree Robotics founder Wang Xingxing: Embodied intelligence tipping point may arrive within one to two years
key_facts: Unitree Robotics founder Wang Xingxing said on 12 Oct 2026 in Shanghai that, as AI model capabilities rapidly improve, the tipping point for embodied intelligence may arrive within one to two years.
He spoke at the opening ceremony of the 26th China International Industry Fair; he is chairman, general manager and chief technology officer of Unitree.

He said major AI updates occur every one to two months and that GPT-6's release has raised awareness among embodied-intelligence practitioners; Unitree has deployed it on various robots for task testing with 'very impressive' results.
He said next year's launch of GPT-7 could directly 'break through' the core challenges of embodied intelligence.

He acknowledged that several Chinese and foreign robotics companies have started factory pilot programs, but large-scale use still requires solving generalization and efficiency; he believes this can be done within the next few years.
He expects commercial service uses to progress faster than industrial ones, and home uses to lag further behind.
He said his biggest mistake of the past decade-plus was not believing in AI strongly enough.

multiple robotics companies—both in China and abroad—have launched pilot programs in factory settings, but large-scale application still requires overcoming two key bottlenecks: generalization capability and efficiency.

why_it_matters_hint: A leading robot-company founder expects embodied AI to take off within one to two years, but it is a forecast from someone who sells robots, with no new test data.
event_date: 12 Oct 2026 (opening ceremony, China International Industry Fair, Shanghai)
notes: BigGo Finance wrote the piece and credits no other outlet; quotes are translated. The closing paragraph is BigGo's own commentary on investment effects and is not used. Google News listings (headlines only) show Wang gave earlier timelines: 'ChatGPT moment' in two to three years (19-20 Aug 2026) and an 'inflection point is near' (27 Sep 2026), so the one-to-two-year figure is a shorter estimate; not verified from article text.
